parts: At noon, a class measures a pole's shadow as 45 centimetres. Two hours later, the shadow is longer.
Explain why a changing shadow does not mean that the pole has grown.
A recipe uses three quarters of a cup of flour. Mira prepares half of the recipe.
Describe how the amount of flour changes without treating the cup size as a different unit.
A model cliff shows 5 undisturbed layers of sediment. The teacher asks which layer was deposited first.
In this simplified example, lower layers are older; disturbed rocks can require more evidence.
A classroom circuit contains a 3-volt battery, a bulb and an open switch.
The bulb does not light because the path is incomplete, even though the battery is connected.
Clap twice, pause, then clap twice again. Repeat this pattern for 4 rounds.
The repeated instruction is intentional; distinguish the number of claps from the number of rounds.
A fictional weather chart records 0 millimetres of rain on Monday and 20 millimetres on Tuesday.
No rain on one day does not show that the instrument failed. Compare the observations before drawing a conclusion.
Every square has 4 equal sides, but not every shape with four equal sides is a square.
A conclusion about all members of a group needs stronger support than an example about one member.
In a fictional story, Asha tells Ravi that she found 2 notebooks beside the window.
Keep the speaker, listener and owner distinct when retelling the event; the sentence does not identify the owner.
